items.title: Thiruparankundram pillar a British-era survey marker says report| LME 181 | Pooja Prasanna
items.summary: On November 24, the Karthigai Deepam lamp was lit at the disputed stone pillar on top of the Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai. Tamil Nadu instead witnessed a tense situation between the police, BJP and Hindutva groups The stone pillar on a hill in Madurai has been at the centre of a heated religious and political dispute for a while now. The pillar stands 50 metres away from the Sikandar Badusha Dargah on Thiruparankundram hill. Hindutva groups have secured court judgments that allow a lamp lit here during the annual Karthigai Deepam festival. But the Tamil Nadu government and temple administration have argued that the pillar is not a traditional lamp-lighting structure, but an old survey marker. Now, a new report by the state government appears to offer evidence for that claim. It identifies the disputed pillar as part of a massive 200-year old British-era project to map the Indian subcontinent The report in fact documents hundreds of similar survey stations across Tamil Nadu, some of which have since become places of worship. items.summary: The Bombay High Court recently held that that the Industrial Development Bank of India Limited (IDBI) was not a government company or a government undertaking [Mrinmayee Umrotkar v. Union of India].
